Hi Sophie — thanks for the procurement form and the timeline. I pulled together a concise unit-econ comparison to make the trade-offs explicit. Summary first, details below.

Quick summary (assumptions: medium-compute LLMs, average response size ~350 tokens, 99th p95 latency target):
- Hosted (Redwood multi-tenant, US region): ~ $300 per 1M tokens baseline.
- Hosted (Redwood multi-tenant, EU region): baseline + ~18% => ~ $354 per 1M tokens (increased infra & inter-region egress + compliance overhead).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity, 12-month commit): US ~ $240 per 1M tokens; EU ~ $276 per 1M tokens. Dedicated needs commit but gives 20–25% uplift on unit economics.
- Private (customer-managed cloud/VPC or on-prem): estimate ~ $220–$260 per 1M tokens but includes customer infra & ops — best for strong regulatory controls, upfront work for deployment.

Notes on the EU premium:
- Primary drivers: higher instance pricing in certain EU zones, double-logging for audit copies, and stricter retention/deletion pipelines that add operational cost. We amortize that across token units which is why you see a 15–20% delta.
- For a 5M tokens/mo pilot, difference vs US-hosted is ~$270/month at the $354 figure vs $300 baseline; at 12M tokens the delta becomes more material (~$1,200/month).

Recommended path for Finova given requirements & runway:
1) Pilot: EU-hosted with strict DPA + 1-month price lock; 5M tokens cap to validate quality and performance.
2) If performance and residency checks pass, move to a 12-month Dedicated commit (recommended at expected 10–12M/mo) to capture the lower per-token rate.
3) For regulated PII-heavy flows, evaluate Private deployment — we can scope infra + TCO in a separate SOW.

Attached: a short spreadsheet with line-item math and a draft SOW that calls out DPA/GDPR clauses we usually include. If you’d like, we can convert the pilot into a short purchase order + statement of work and route for signature this week.
